justification: Repairs CI rather than served output: adds the missing PyMuPDF test dependency, removes pytest fail-fast, scopes the QA-report job to pull requests (it is structurally unpassable on main), and adds a red-main alarm plus a dependency-skip ratchet. No product code, no DB writes, no user-facing text. Standard rather than minor because it changes what the gates verify and therefore what a green tick means.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/ -q --tb=short -p ci_sim  (import blocker denying every module absent from the requirements-test.txt closure) ; python scripts/check_dependency_skips.py ; gh run view 30856789737 --log-failed
falsifiable_check.passes_when: The whole suite runs to completion under CI's exact import surface with 0 failures (3665 passed), the four TestExtractorSelectionRules tests among them; the dependency-skip census reports 23 against a baseline of 23; and no job in gates.yml can be red-by-construction on main.
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any test fails under the SIMULATED CI import surface — that is the real condition, because the whole outage was a module present locally and absent in CI, and a plain local run cannot see it (this machine has PyMuPDF installed, which is why 3698 tests passed here on 08-06 while main had already been red for three days). The ratchet goes red if the skip count rises, if a new dependency starts skipping tests, or if .pytest-skips.json is absent — a missing census is failure, never zero.
falsifiable_check.demonstrated_failing: All four states reproduced red before the fix. (1) With the CI import blocker and no PyMuPDF the suite reports exactly 4 failures, all ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fitz'. (2) The real CI log for run 30856789737 shows the identical failure and '1 failed, 1405 passed, 1 skipped, 19 deselected' — 1,405 of 3,665 tests ran, ~2,260 did not. (3) The ratchet was fed a doctored census three ways: new dependency -> exit 1, rising count on a known dependency -> exit 1, missing report -> exit 2, unchanged -> exit 0. (4) gh run list --workflow gates.yml --branch main returns five consecutive failures dated 2026-08-03, confirming the outage independently of the report of it.
falsifiable_check.mutation_evidence: Restore -x to the pytest step -> the run again reports only the first failure and says nothing about the remaining ~2,260 tests. Remove PyMuPDF from requirements-test.txt -> the 4 failures return under the blocker. Delete the pytest_terminal_summary hook -> .pytest-skips.json is never written and check_dependency_skips.py exits 2 rather than silently passing. Drop the pull_request guard on qa-and-liability -> it fails on every main push on the squash-merge hash mismatch and main can never be green. Sol round 2: loosen the ratchet back to `count > limit` -> the recovered-then-regressed case passes again; count only classified skips -> a 'requires boto3' skip is invisible again. Sol round 3: compare only the totals -> the offsetting shapely/icontract trade passes again; restore the auto-write on a missing baseline -> deleting the file passes with an inflated baseline. Sol round 4: gate the whole qa-and-liability job on pull_request -> a direct main push is unscanned; treat a missing total_skipped as 'no opinion' -> the unrecognised-skip axis switches off silently; swallow the census write error -> the ratchet reads the previous run's numbers. Sol round 5: use HEAD^ as the main-push scan base -> an earlier commit in a multi-commit push goes unscanned; restore the >50h clock rule -> the alarm cries wolf every Monday.
falsifiable_check.self_comparison_note: This does not re-run the code and check it agrees with itself. The import surface is derived from requirements-test.txt through pip's own resolver (48 packages), not from whatever happens to be installed here, and the outcome is cross-checked against the actual GitHub Actions log rather than a local re-execution.

pre_impl.existing_data: gh run list shows gates failing on main on 0c41c09d, 8b9b0ea7, 03bc720a, 2b7dcd97 and 412a3788, all 2026-08-03. The latest run's jobs: Python tests FAILED, QA report + liability FAILED, Jest / Duplication / Schema contract passed. Its log gives the exact cause (fitz at tests/test_dcp_as_at.py:358) and the exact damage. The CI import surface was resolved with pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --report against requirements-test.txt: 48 packages, no PyMuPDF, no shapely, no matplotlib, no icontract, no requests.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Two premises in the brief needed correcting. (a) '~1,800 tests haven't executed' — the log says 1,405 ran of 3,665, so ~2,260 did not. (b) The fitz failure was not the only thing holding main red: qa-and-liability was failing independently on a squash-merge hash mismatch, so fixing PyMuPDF alone would have left main red and the new alarm firing on day one. Also: PyMuPDF CAN be a CI dependency, so the brief's fallback clause does not apply to it — pymupdf-1.28.0-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl is an abi3 wheel covering CI's Python 3.12 with no system libraries, and requirements.txt:120 already pins the same version.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The ratchet deliberately mirrors the repo's existing idiom (scripts/check_test_baselines.py, brief_field_coverage_ratchet.py, jscpd, schema_contract_baseline.json): a committed baseline that may only shrink. It could not extend either of those, because both ratchet numbers that a skipped test still contributes to — skips are exactly what they cannot see. The alarm workflow is new; nothing in .github/ watched main's own health, and the only prior signal was a red X addressed to nobody.

functions.name: pytest_terminal_summary
functions.input: pytest's terminal reporter after the run, i.e. every skip report the session produced
functions.output: writes .pytest-skips.json and prints a 'TESTS THAT DID NOT RUN' section grouped by the missing module
functions.if_none: no dependency skips -> the file records count 0 and no section prints; the ratchet then compares 0 against the baseline

functions.name: _dependency_from_skip_reason
functions.input: a single skip reason string from a skip report
functions.output: the module name the skip blames, or None when the skip is about something else entirely
functions.if_none: env-gated skips such as 'set RUN_LIVE_GEMINI=1' return None deliberately — counting a deliberate opt-out would make the ratchet measure intent instead of coverage

functions.name: main
functions.input: the .pytest-skips.json census and the committed dependency-skip-baseline.json
functions.output: a printed census grouped by dependency, and exit 0, 1 or 2
functions.if_none: a missing census exits 2 — 'no report' and 'no skips' must not look the same, which is the failure mode being fixed

values.if_missing: treated as failure, never as zero

values.guard_at: the empty-RUN_JSON branch in the same step
values.if_missing: state=broken — no completed run is unknown, and unknown about a gate is not health

values.value: age of the latest successful run
values.if_missing: n/a — a green run older than 50h is itself treated as broken, so a workflow that quietly stopped firing cannot read as healthy

queries.purpose: find the newest completed gates run on main
queries.if_zero: state=broken, noting the workflow may be disabled or may never have run
queries.if_wrong: a stale-but-green run older than 50h also trips the alarm, so the two ways of being unverified are both covered

queries.purpose: find an already-open alarm issue so a long outage is one thing, not seventy-two
queries.where_clause: state open, exact title match in jq
queries.if_wrong: a title-only match could in principle collide with a human-filed issue of the same name; the consequence is a comment on that issue rather than a duplicate, which is the safe direction

break_it.scenario: a dependency goes missing again and the test using it sits inside pytest.importorskip rather than importing directly
break_it.what_happens: the test skips instead of failing, CI stays green, and the coverage disappears with no signal — the silent half of this same outage, and how 23 tests came to never run anywhere
break_it.how: the conftest census counts dependency skips and the ratchet fails on any increase or any new dependency name
break_it.repro: append a fabricated skip to .pytest-skips.json and run python scripts/check_dependency_skips.py — exits 1

break_it.scenario: main breaks and nobody looks at the Actions tab
break_it.what_happens: exactly what happened: three days red, ~2,260 tests unexecuted, every merge landing on an unverified base
break_it.how: main-red-alarm opens a GitHub issue within minutes of a failed gates run on main and closes it when main goes green; the job also fails, so the alarm is visible in the Actions list too
break_it.repro: workflow_dispatch the alarm while main is red — it files the issue, which it would do today

break_it.scenario: the newest completed gates run on main cannot be found, or is green but stale — the gates workflow stopped running at all (disabled, quota exhausted, trigger edited away)
break_it.what_happens: no failure event is ever emitted, an event-driven alarm stays silent, and absence looks identical to health
break_it.how: the daily scheduled sweep asserts a recent AND successful run, treating both 'no completed run' and 'succeeded but >50h ago' as broken
break_it.repro: read the Assess main step: the empty-RUN_JSON and AGE_H>50 branches both set state=broken

break_it.scenario: the alarm becomes the noise that gets ignored
break_it.what_happens: a fresh issue per failed run trains people to filter it — the same learned blindness in a new place
break_it.how: one issue reused by title: later failures comment on it rather than duplicating, and a green run closes it
break_it.repro: the Raise step searches for the open issue and comments when it finds one

break_it.scenario: PyMuPDF is installed but the four tests do not really exercise anything
break_it.what_happens: the dependency lands, CI goes green, and the fix is cosmetic
break_it.how: the four tests generate real PDFs and assert extracted dates (2026-03-05, 2024-09-18 and two None cases), and the module under test opens those PDFs with fitz at scripts/extract_dcp_stated_dates.py:95,139 — the real extraction path, not a stub

break_it.what_happens: a real cost is traded for the diagnostic gain and nobody checks whether it was worth it
break_it.how: measured: the full suite runs in ~12s locally and ~10s in the last CI log, inside a job dominated by setup and pip install. The saving -x bought was negligible; the information it destroyed was three days of it.
break_it.repro: the timing line on any run: '3665 passed ... in 12.62s'

break_it.scenario: the qa-and-liability job is skipped on main and something real stops being checked
break_it.what_happens: a genuine gate is quietly narrowed under cover of a CI repair
break_it.how: nothing is lost: the QA report binds to the PR's commits, and the liability scan diffs against merge-base, which on main is HEAD — an empty diff. Both questions are answerable only before the merge and both still run there. On main the job now reads 'skipped' instead of a red that could never be anything else.
break_it.repro: the job's if: condition plus scripts/qa_gate.py:1285-1302, which requires the report hash to be among the branch's last 5 commits

break_it.scenario: a dependency is installed, skips fall 23 -> 18, the baseline is left loose, and a later change removes the dependency again
break_it.what_happens: both runs pass the ratchet, so five recovered tests stop running a second time — silently, which is the exact disease
break_it.how: Sol finding, verified real and fixed: the ratchet matches EXACTLY, both directions. An improvement fails the build until the baseline is tightened in the same commit, where a reviewer sees it. A ratchet left loose is not a ratchet.
break_it.repro: remove the shapely entries from .pytest-skips.json without touching the baseline and run scripts/check_dependency_skips.py — exits 1

break_it.scenario: a test is skipped with a reason no pattern recognises, e.g. skipif(boto3 is None, reason='requires boto3')
break_it.what_happens: the classifier matches nothing, the dependency census records no new skip, CI stays green and the coverage is lost — the same hole one rephrasing away
break_it.how: Sol finding, verified real and fixed: conftest now records EVERY skip, and the baseline pins the total (25) as well as the classified subset (23). An unrecognised skip trips the total ratchet and is printed by name and reason, so classification is a diagnostic aid rather than the thing enforcement depends on.
break_it.repro: append a skip with dependency=None to .pytest-skips.json and run the script — exits 1 and names the test

break_it.scenario: offsetting drift — one new test skips for shapely (13->14) while one icontract test is recovered (5->4)
break_it.what_happens: the classified count stays 23, the total stays 25, no dependency name is new, and newly lost coverage passes green — the ratchet cancels itself out
break_it.how: Sol finding, verified real and fixed: per-dependency counts are compared exactly, so either half of that trade trips the gate on its own. Totals are now the third axis rather than the only one.
break_it.repro: reassign one icontract skip to shapely in .pytest-skips.json and run the script — exits 1 naming both movements

break_it.scenario: dependency-skip-baseline.json is deleted or absent while extra tests are skipping
break_it.what_happens: the script wrote a fresh baseline from the run it was judging and exited 0 — deleting the file becomes a way to bless whatever is broken today, and the gate certifies its own input
break_it.how: Sol finding, verified real and fixed: a missing baseline exits 2 unless --init is passed explicitly, so generating one is a deliberate, reviewable act rather than a side effect of a red run.
break_it.repro: mv dependency-skip-baseline.json away and run the script — exits 2

break_it.scenario: a change is pushed directly to main containing prohibited liability wording
break_it.what_happens: scoping the whole qa-and-liability job to pull requests — my first attempt at the squash-merge fix — meant an admin push or any write-access automation landed on main with nothing scanning it. I introduced this while fixing something else.
break_it.how: Sol finding, verified real and fixed: only the QA-REPORT step is PR-gated. The liability scan runs on both events, diffing merge-base on a PR and HEAD^..HEAD on a main push, which is exactly the change that landed.
break_it.repro: the step-level if: in gates.yml — the scan has none

break_it.scenario: total_skipped is removed from the baseline or set to null
break_it.what_happens: total_limit became None, the comparison was skipped, and the one axis that catches an unrecognised skip reason switched itself off silently
break_it.how: Sol finding, verified real and fixed: a missing total_skipped exits 2 and says so. Absent is not 'no opinion'.
break_it.repro: delete total_skipped from dependency-skip-baseline.json and run the script — exits 2

break_it.scenario: the pytest run dies before the summary hook fires — a collection error, a cancelled job — or the census cannot be written
break_it.what_happens: the previous run's .pytest-skips.json stays on disk and the ratchet judges this run against stale numbers — and passes
break_it.how: Sol finding, verified real and fixed two ways: pytest_sessionstart deletes any existing census before the run, and a failed write removes the file rather than swallowing the error. The ratchet then exits 2 ('report not found'), which is honest. Verified as a side effect: a PARTIAL run now writes a partial census that fails the ratchet (exit 1) rather than certifying a subset as the whole suite.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_dcp_as_at.py -q then scripts/check_dependency_skips.py — exits 1, not 0

break_it.scenario: an admin pushes several commits to main at once and the prohibited wording is in an earlier one, not the tip
break_it.what_happens: HEAD^..HEAD scans only the last commit of the push, so wording introduced in any earlier commit of the same push is never examined
break_it.how: Sol finding, verified real and fixed: the base is github.event.before, which is the ref as it stood before the whole push, falling back to HEAD^ only when `before` is the all-zero SHA or is unreachable.
break_it.repro: read the else-branch of the Liability language scan step in gates.yml

break_it.scenario: main is green on Friday, nothing is pushed over the weekend, and the Monday sweep fires anyway
break_it.what_happens: the clock-based staleness rule (>50h) opens a red-main issue for a main that is verified and unchanged — a false alarm every Monday, which is precisely how the next real alarm gets ignored. I wrote this one in.
break_it.how: Sol finding, verified real and fixed: staleness is now about COVERAGE, not elapsed time. A successful run whose headSha equals main's current HEAD is green at any age; the alarm fires when HEAD has no completed run and is more than 3h old, which is the state that actually means 'nothing checked this'.
break_it.repro: read the SHA = HEAD_SHA branch in the Assess main step

break_it.scenario: a census file from an earlier run survives into this one and happens to match the baseline
break_it.what_happens: the ratchet reads numbers this run did not produce and exits 0
break_it.how: three layers now: pytest_sessionstart removes it, a failed write removes it, and the CI step rm -f's it before pytest so a file that cannot be removed fails the step visibly instead of being absorbed. Residual, stated: if all three removals fail AND the stale counts match exactly, it would still pass — contrived enough to record rather than engineer around.
break_it.repro: the rm -f in the pytest step, plus pytest_sessionstart in tests/conftest.py

post_merge.db_reset: No. No migration and no DB access added.
post_merge.secrets: None added. The alarm uses the automatic GITHUB_TOKEN with issues:write and actions:read.
post_merge.manual_verify: 1) After merge, watch the gates run on main and confirm every job is green or deliberately skipped: gh run watch $(gh run list --workflow gates.yml --branch main --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId'). 2) Confirm the pytest job now reports ~3,665 tests rather than 1,405, and that the 'TESTS THAT DID NOT RUN' section shows 23. 3) Confirm the alarm closes any issue it opened once main is green. 4) The alarm cannot be fully exercised until main is green at least once — while main is red it is expected to file the issue and fail, which is correct behaviour rather than a regression.
